pages.lesson:
LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Phonological Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological Awareness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What can you do to improve your ability to pronounce words accurately?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological Awareness helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS
Study Phonological Awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological Awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example. (skill: apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological Awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological Awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological Awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Phonological Awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What can you do to improve your ability to pronounce words accurately?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological Awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply appropriate stress and intonation for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
